decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right, pens on the left. Begin right-arm side-grasp orientation with small continuous elbow-up motions; left stays clear.
Move the right wrist outward and forward while finishing the inward-facing side grasp. Keep the left arm parked.
Previous suffix was rejected. Replan from measured pose with reduced translation and yaw increments, advancing toward the holder without forcing a wrist configuration jump.
Back away from wrist singularity by reducing yaw. Switch to a near-side holder grasp instead of forcing the outer-side approach.
No motion was executed on the rejected chunk. Ease out of the near-singular wrist using very small yaw-only steps.
Advance toward the near side of the right-hand holder, reducing wrist yaw and lowering gently with open fingers.
Align the right fingers around the holder from its near side. Approach slowly at mid-wall height; grasp is not yet confirmed.
The holder shifted during approach. Correct the near-side grasp height and back off slightly, then close around the wall; retention will be checked visually.
Recenter slightly toward the holder visible to the right of the fingers, close fully, and make a short vertical retention test.
The holder did not rise with the test. Reopen, lower to the wall midpoint, and advance the fingers farther around it before closing.
Wrist view shows the holder offset to the right of the closing fingers. Recenter laterally with an open grasp, close, then lift only two centimeters to test retention.
The fingers closed in front of the holder rather than around it. Open and advance deeper at mid-wall height, then close without lifting yet.
Hold the closure, then lift and draw back slightly to test whether the holder is retained rather than pushed.
The holder tipped and was not retained. Open and clear it vertically, beginning an overhead recovery grasp without crossing workspaces.
Approach above the fallen holder, rotating the right gripper downward while maintaining clearance and an open aperture.
Use smaller downward-orientation increments after the continuity rejection, lowering toward the fallen holder instead of extending farther upward.
Lower the open fingers a short distance around the fallen holder and close. Keep orientation fixed to avoid additional wrist folding.
The forward overhead target was rejected. Withdraw the wrist and use a shallower approach angle to restore joint margin while keeping fingers above the holder.
No motion occurred in the rejected chunk. Reduce withdrawal and rotation increments substantially to leave the near-singular configuration continuously.
Back away upward with fixed orientation to regain reach margin before attempting further grasping.
Withdraw toward the robot while easing the wrist back from the overhead posture, preserving continuous joint motion.
Clear the holder and bring the wrist back and upward with fixed orientation to regain a less folded configuration.
Align the open right gripper over the fallen holder using small wrist rotations and forward translation; preserve the raised elbow and verify alignment before descending.
After the interrupted prefix, use much smaller increments to center the overhead fingers and lower toward the holder, with no closure until alignment is visible.
Hold wrist orientation and height after the rejection, using sub-millimeter translations to improve alignment without forcing an IK branch change.
Translation remains IK-limited. Keep position fixed and make a small yaw adjustment to move away from the nearly singular wrist before resuming the recovery.
Use a shallower approach to the fallen holder instead of forcing farther forward reach. Lower while drawing the wrist slightly toward the robot, keeping the fingers open.
The prior command executed zero steps. Reduce the coupled lowering and wrist adjustment fourfold to preserve joint continuity.
The lowering path remains continuity-limited. Withdraw upward and toward the robot with fixed orientation to regain a safer configuration.
Ease the wrist out of the highly folded overhead posture while withdrawing, keeping the open fingers clear of the fallen holder.
The previous command executed nothing and slightly exceeded joint continuity. Halve each withdrawal and wrist increment, starting from the unchanged measured pose.
Continue a slow retreat and reduce downward wrist pitch, avoiding a large configuration change before attempting another holder approach.
Keep the wrist location fixed and introduce a gradual yaw offset to avoid the nearly aligned wrist singularity before translating again.
Ease the wrist out of the strongly downward posture while lowering slightly in place, seeking a continuous, less constrained side approach.
Translate the open fingers toward the holder seen at the upper-right of the wrist view, holding orientation fixed and descending gradually.
Continue visual centering toward the holder with fixed wrist attitude and open fingers; the previous motion improved wrist-view alignment but did not establish a grasp.
The holder is now between the wrist-view finger boundaries. Make a small lateral/forward correction without further descent, then close for a recovery grasp.
The holder is visibly centered at the closing fingers. Maintain full closure and lift gently with a short retreat to check retention.
The holder remained on the table. Reopen and reach farther around its body, rather than closing only at the near end; keep the wrist attitude fixed.
The fingers now reach along the holder body. Correct a small lateral offset, close, and perform a short vertical lift to assess retention.
The lift again left the holder on the table. Reopen and reposition the grasp center lower and toward the holder using the head-view geometry, rather than relying only on wrist centering.
At the lower approach height, make a small centering adjustment and close around the holder. Lift briefly to check whether this grasp retains it.
The holder appears between the closed fingers, but retention is uncertain. Lift and retreat gently while starting a small upright rotation; verify that it follows.
The holder slipped away and moved left. Reopen and approach its new head-view location, correcting the grasp center lower and left while keeping orientation fixed.

The descent was interrupted with a substantial tracking residual. Replan at the measured pose, adjusting wrist pitch slowly and advancing only a millimeter per step to leave the joint-limited posture.
Use the head-view holder location to approach more vertically, shifting left and forward while increasing downward pitch. Keep fingers open and motion continuous.
Continue a slow, nearly vertical descent to the fallen holder’s midpoint, compensating for the changing finger offset while keeping the gripper open.
Shift the open fingers toward the holder’s upper-right wrist-view offset at constant height, then close and pause before testing retention.
The translation suffix was rejected before closure. Close at the latest observed alignment, pause, and make a small vertical retention test without further forward reach.
The holder is not retained and shifted left. Reopen and correct the grasp laterally using the head view, with slight withdrawal to avoid the forward-reach limit.
Make a small forward/right correction with slight clearance, then close and settle at the holder rather than lifting during closure.
The forward overhead path is continuity-limited. Change to a shallower approach while shifting toward the holder’s rightward wrist-view location, keeping fingers open.
Back the open gripper toward the head-view holder center, correcting for the link6-to-finger offset and improving clearance before another closure.
Use the observed wrist-view response to bring the holder down and left between the open fingers, maintaining the current wrist attitude.
Advance laterally and slightly forward to place more of the holder body between the jaws, then close without lifting.
Maintain full closure and test the grasp with a slow vertical lift, leaving orientation fixed so retention can be judged from the holder’s motion.
The holder still sits beyond the fingertips. Reopen and advance along the gripper approach axis to enclose the body more deeply, then close and pause.
Settle the closed grasp and make a small upward/backward retention test. Do not infer grasp success from the closure command alone.
The holder was not retained. Reopen and move the grasp center lower and left toward the body seen in the head view, keeping orientation fixed.
The forward descent is IK-limited. Change to a shallower near-side grasp while withdrawing the wrist and lowering, keeping the fingers open and the motion continuous.
The prior command executed no motion. Reduce the coupled wrist and withdrawal increments fourfold to preserve joint continuity while leaving the constrained posture.
No motion executed in the last attempt. Further reduce the increments below the observed continuity limit and ease toward a shallower grasp.
Continue toward a shallow side grasp while bringing the wrist back and down. Keep the open fingers clear and monitor continuity.
Replan from the measured height after the rejected descent. Translate at fixed attitude to center the near end of the holder, then close and pause.
Allow the closure to settle around the visible holder, then lift and retreat slightly at fixed orientation to test retention.
The holder is still on the table. Open and lift away to clear the constrained low posture before replanning the recovery.
Increase clearance and gradually adjust the wrist for an overhead recovery, keeping the left arm parked and all motions continuous.
Reduce the clearance and orientation increments fourfold after the continuity rejection, replanning from the measured pose.
The upward path is reach-limited. Retract toward the robot while rotating downward, rather than increasing extension; keep the holder clear and gripper open.
The prior chunk moved neither arm. Halve the retreat and rotation increments to stay below the measured joint-change limit.
The coupled rotation is continuity-limited. Hold attitude fixed and withdraw toward the robot with a gradual descent to regain maneuvering margin.
No movement occurred on the rejected chunk. Use sub-millimeter fixed-attitude withdrawal increments near the continuity boundary.
With continuity margin restored, lower at fixed attitude and shift left toward the holder’s near end. Keep fingers open for visual alignment.
Lower while increasing downward pitch and moving forward slightly, keeping the estimated finger center over the holder and avoiding the previous shallow-posture limit.
Hold attitude after the rejected rotation, making a small rightward and downward correction toward the visible holder before closing and pausing.
The near end remains outside the jaw center. Reopen and advance deeper around the body with a shallower angle, monitoring the reach limit.
The forward translation was rejected. Keep the measured wrist position fixed and ease toward a shallower approach to restore reach margin before translating again.
No action executed in the rejected chunk. Withdraw in small fixed-attitude steps first, then use a much smaller wrist adjustment.
Replan after the one-step prefix. Test a very small vertical-only approach at fixed orientation, avoiding the rejected combined withdrawal direction.
Lower the open fingers slightly farther and correct left toward the holder’s near end in the head view, then close and settle without lifting.
Settle full closure, then lift and retreat a few centimeters at fixed attitude to test whether the holder follows the fingers.
The holder did not follow the lift. Reopen and correct the rightward, distant wrist-view offset, advancing around the body rather than closing ahead of it.
The forward suffix was rejected. Recenter using the head-view holder position and estimated finger offset, moving left and back at fixed height to regain reach margin.
Correct the apparent vertical and forward offset of the finger contact region, then close and settle at the holder without lifting.
Reopen and correct toward the holder’s rightward offset while making the approach shallower. The previous closure did not enclose the holder.
Advance the fingers slightly right and forward around the near end while easing wrist pitch, then close without lifting.
Keep full closure while it settles, then lift vertically four centimeters at fixed attitude to check whether the holder is retained.
Retention remains uncertain. Keep closure and withdraw slowly toward the robot at fixed attitude, checking whether the holder follows rather than assuming a successful grasp.
The holder did not follow. Clear it and change the jaw alignment to grasp across its shorter dimension, rather than repeatedly closing near the end.
Continue aligning the jaws across the holder width, translating left and forward while lowering gently. The right arm remains in its own workspace.
With the jaw orientation changed, correct toward the holder at the upper-left of the wrist view while lowering at fixed attitude.
After the rejected forward descent, withdraw slightly and ease downward pitch with small coupled increments, preserving an open grasp and joint continuity.
The last chunk executed zero steps. Reduce the coupled wrist and withdrawal increments to forty percent, starting from the unchanged observed pose.
With the changed jaw alignment, lower a short distance toward the holder and shift left, then close without lifting so enclosure can be inspected.
The holder remains beyond the fingers. Reopen and advance gently while leveling the approach, avoiding another closure in front of the body.
The near end is now visible beside the left finger. Shift toward it and lower slowly at the leveled attitude before attempting enclosure.
The forward descent reached a continuity boundary. Replan from the executed prefix, turning the open gripper toward the leftward holder while withdrawing slightly.
The prior command executed zero steps. Reduce the coupled yaw and withdrawal increments to stay below the joint-continuity limit.
